title: Paloma and the Ghost
premise: When Flight 4471 to Frankfurt vanishes from every radar, booking, and government database while still airborne, private security contractor Coral Ishikawa realizes she was the last person to speak with its pilot — a man who once saved her life and who was carrying evidence that three governments would rather erase than expose. Hunted by an assassin codenamed Vesper and betrayed by the agency that rewrote her own contracts, Coral must reconstruct the flight's true cargo from fragments of memory, forged records, and one surviving passenger. The truth — a laundering scheme built on erased people, not just erased planes — gets out minutes before the Frankfurt markets open, collapsing the network but costing Coral her old identity; in the end she chooses a new name and a new belonging among the survivors the system tried to delete.
about_author: Isandro Sterling is the pen name of a former aviation-logistics analyst who spent a decade inside the paperwork of companies that preferred not to exist. Sterling writes thrillers about the violence hidden in ledgers and lives in Lisbon with a rescue dog named Ledger.

chapters.title: Rules That Keep Moving
chapters.summary: Coral Ishikawa's POV. A routine protection detail in Geneva goes sideways when her client's contract is retroactively voided mid-assignment, stranding her without legal cover. She navigates the fallout with cold professionalism, but the reader sees the toll: five years of rewritten rules have hollowed out any sense of home. Emotional beat: weary competence masking quiet dread.

chapters.title: The Last Call
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. An old friend, pilot Daniel Okafor, calls at 2 a.m. asking her to verify a manifest he can't explain — then the line dies. Hours later, Flight 4471 vanishes from every record while still transmitting altitude data. Coral realizes she may be the only living person who remembers it existed. Emotional beat: vertigo as reality itself becomes unreliable.

chapters.title: Nobody on Board
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At Geneva airport, airline staff genuinely have no flight 4471 in their systems; a gate agent's face flickers with something like fear when Coral presses. She retrieves Daniel's backup drive from a locker using their old shared code. Emotional beat: gaslighting sharpening into resolve — she refuses to doubt her own memory.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Assassin Vesper's POV, first time. Elegant, methodical, we watch them receive the kill list: everyone who touched Flight 4471's paper trail. Coral's name is third. Vesper notes with professional interest that someone above them is frightened enough to skip protocol. Emotional beat: chilling calm, the machinery of erasure made human.

chapters.title: The Locker Code
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The drive holds partial flight logs and a voicemail: Daniel suspected the plane carried no cargo but passengers — people being moved off the books between jurisdictions. Coral decodes his route through Zurich contacts, aware she's now racing a clock she can't see. Emotional beat: grief for Daniel braided with purpose.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: a Swiss intelligence officer, a German financial regulator, and a US Treasury attaché, each independently discovering their agency signed off on 4471's erasure — and each deciding to bury it. The reader sees the conspiracy's architecture before Coral does. Emotional beat: institutional cowardice, banal and vast.

chapters.title: Rewritten
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Her own employment history begins dissolving — old clients deny hiring her, her security clearances return errors. She understands: erasing the flight means erasing witnesses, and she's been pre-flagged. She burns her apartment's records and goes mobile. Emotional beat: loss of identity as literal threat; belonging stripped away.

chapters.title: Zurich Station
chapters.summary: Coral's POV meets a former colleague, Marek, who owes Daniel a debt and provides safe passage — but Coral catches him photographing her documents. Trust becomes a calculation. First near-miss with Vesper in the station's underpass. Emotional beat: paranoia as survival skill; loneliness deepening.

chapters.title: The Passenger Manifest
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Decrypted files reveal nine names aboard 4471 — whistleblowers and witnesses quietly disappeared via a 'repatriation' program. One name has a surviving relative in Basel: Elena Vasquez, whose sister was aboard. Coral decides finding Elena matters more than reaching safety. Emotional beat: the abstract crime gains faces; moral commitment crystallizes.

chapters.title: Basel, Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Elena Vasquez's POV. A grieving accountant who noticed impossible money flows before her sister vanished, Elena has been documenting everything in a notebook no database can hack. Coral arrives; suspicion gives way to alliance. Vesper closes in but hesitates when they see Elena's ordinary kitchen life. Emotional beat: two kinds of memory — digital and handwritten — joining forces.

chapters.title: What the Markets Knew
chapters.summary: Frankfurt regulator Ingrid Halvorsen's POV. She traces short positions placed against companies tied to the repatriation program hours before 4471 'never existed' — proof insiders monetized the erasure itself. She faces a choice: file the report or become the next deleted person. Emotional beat: conscience versus career, the theme of corrupted power embodied.

chapters.title: The Interrogation Room
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Lured by a fake offer of protection, Coral is detained by Swiss officers coached by unseen hands. They offer reinstatement if she recants her memory of the call with Daniel. She performs compliance while passing Elena's notebook location to Marek. Emotional beat: performance under pressure; power trying to purchase her past.

chapters.title: Vesper's Doubt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Reviewing Coral's file, Vesper finds anomalies — Coral herself appears in an old erasure order, survived one years ago. The assassin recognizes a fellow survivor of the machine they serve. They delay the hit, falsifying a report for the first time in their career. Emotional beat: the instrument of power developing a hairline fracture.

chapters.title: Marek's Price
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Marek sells her location to buy his family's safety — but slips Coral the real handoff point first, choosing redemption over survival. His betrayal-and-gift forces Coral to confront what she'd sacrifice for belonging. Emotional beat: betrayal that hurts because it's understandable.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes to Open
chapters.summary: Coral and Elena race toward Frankfurt as European markets prepare to open, where a shell company's quarterly filing will legally bury all 4471 evidence forever. Ingrid, having chosen conscience, sends them the filing's vulnerability window. Three storylines converge. Emotional beat: ticking-clock urgency fused with fragile, improvised trust.

chapters.title: Vesper Intercepted
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ordered to eliminate everyone including Ingrid, Vesper instead feeds their handlers false coordinates and confronts Coral directly — not to kill her, but to ask what she knows about surviving erasure. An armed standoff becomes an uneasy truce. Emotional beat: the hunter seeking absolution; power's tool turning witness.

chapters.title: The Filing Floor
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Inside the Frankfurt exchange's administrative wing, Coral and Elena inject the passenger manifest and flight logs into the public disclosure queue seconds before the shell company's filing locks. Alarms sound. Vesper covers their exit against incoming agency cleaners. Emotional beat: climax — truth as an act of physical courage, paid for in blood.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. As Frankfurt opens, the leaked records cascade: short positions unravel, the repatriation program's architects scramble, and three governments begin publicly blaming each other. Ingrid watches her suppressed report vindicated. Daniel's posthumous data becomes headline fact. Emotional beat: cathartic collapse of the corrupt edifice — power exposed cannot hold.

chapters.title: Cleanup Crew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The network's enforcers turn inward, hunting loose ends including Vesper. Vesper chooses exposure over loyalty, delivering internal orders to journalists — completing the arc from instrument to defector. A final confrontation leaves Vesper wounded but free of the list. Emotional beat: costly liberation; corruption devours itself.

chapters.title: Hearings and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Weeks later, parliamentary hearings grind forward; some architects fall, others retreat into consulting firms. Coral testifies, but learns justice here is partial — Daniel will never be officially acknowledged. Grief without closure. Emotional beat: sober realism about systemic change; mourning that refuses cynicism.

chapters.title: Elena's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In Basel, Elena offers Coral the thing no contract ever did: a place at her table, a community of the program's surviving relatives rebuilding lives together. Coral, whose records are still smoke, accepts a new beginning unrecorded by any database — belonging chosen, not assigned. Emotional beat: warmth earned through fire; the theme of belonging resolved.

chapters.title: Paloma
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Coral's POV. She takes a new name — Paloma, the dove Daniel once joked suited her better than 'Ishikawa' — and visits a memorial the governments refuse to build, a bench overlooking Frankfurt's skyline with nine names carved by hand. Somewhere, Vesper sends an anonymous tip ensuring the last architect faces trial. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; memory as the one record that cannot be erased.
